401892816.summary: No track: not a top-7 vs bottom-7 game (Ottawa is a top-5 power team). Every preview found backs Carolina, which ESPN/DraftKings price at -265 (about 73%). The reasons given: Carolina leads the league in goals for (4.12) and against (2.20), is 8-1-2 at home, and is rested, while Ottawa played at Tampa Bay on Nov 27. Ottawa's power play is last in the league at 12.5%, though the Senators are 7-1-2 in their last 10. Goalies are unconfirmed: Daily Faceoff lists Kochetkov (13-1-1, .911) and Ullmark, but Ullmark started Friday, so Pick Dawgz expects Samuel Ersson (.869). Carolina's Ehlers and K'Andre Miller are day-to-day. The only split is on margin: one model projects a tight 2.2-1.7 game, another 5-2.

401892813.summary: No track: not a top-7 vs bottom-7 game. The few previews out so far all back New Jersey to win, at about -190 to -205. They point to the Devils' 11-3 home record, their scoring (3.68 goals and 32.6 shots a game against Winnipeg's 3.15 and 26.5) and three straight wins. Winnipeg is hot too: 4-0-1 in its last five by one count, and it beat the Devils 4-2 on Nov 10. The main worry for New Jersey is its penalty kill (67.8%) against Winnipeg's 22.7% power play. Both teams won on Friday night, so both are on the second half of a back-to-back. With Jake Allen used Friday, Connor Hellebuyck is the likely Devils starter, though nobody has confirmed it. Winnipeg's starter is unclear: Skinner played Friday. The one projection has the game close, 1.8-1.5 in goals.

401892810.summary: No track: not a top-7 vs bottom-7 game. The market makes Vegas only a short home favorite (DraftKings VGK -122 / MTL +102, total 6.5). Bang the Book and Picks and Parlays back Vegas, mainly for its 27.5% power play against Montreal's 13.5%. Montreal has lost three straight and scored four goals in them, including a 6-0 loss at Colorado. Vegas is on a back-to-back after losing 4-1 at San Jose on Friday; Carter Hart started that game, so Adin Hill is expected in goal (unconfirmed). Captain Mark Stone left Friday's game and is being evaluated; Hanifin and Pietrangelo are out. Montreal is missing Demidov, Matheson, Anderson and Kreider, and Guhle is day-to-day. Pick Dawgz and Parlae's projection lean Montreal, citing the back-to-back, Montreal's 9-3-1 road record and a bounce-back spot.
